issues.description: `Course` uses the instructor concept inconsistently: the problem statement and template define a property/initializer label `instructor`, but the solution defines the property and initializer label as `lecturer`. This breaks consistency and also causes downstream code to reference a non-existent `instructor` property in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use `instructor` consistently across all artifacts: in the solution, rename `lecturer` to `instructor`, change the initializer to `init(name:instructor:ratings:)`, and update all references accordingly.

issues.description: In the solution repository, `Client` constructs `Course` with the argument label `instructor:`, but `Course`'s initializer is declared with the label `lecturer:`. This is a compile-time error in Swift and prevents the solution from building.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the initializer label match the call site (preferred: `instructor:` per the problem statement), or update the call site and all other references to use `lecturer:` consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement requires `Course` to be `public` with `public` properties (`name`, `instructor`) and to be initializable from outside the module, but both template and solution declare `name`/`instructor` (or `lecturer`), `ratings`, and the initializer without `public`, making them `internal` and not accessible from other modules (e.g., `DeveloperApp` or external tests).
issues.suggestedFix: Align access control with the specification: declare `public let name`, `public let instructor`, `public var ratings`, and `public init(...)` (and the chosen instructor/lecturer name) so the API is usable outside `DeveloperLib`.
